column1: # Companion to sim/mutation_harness_audit.tsv.  That file records whether a
# harness reports a zero-match anchor honestly.  This one records whether
# anything ever RUNS it, what an exit code from it would mean, and what wiring
# it as a sim/regress.sh row would cost.
# sched       SCHEDULED / UNSCHEDULED / UNCERTAIN.  MEASURED 2026-09-20 by:
#             (2) regress.sh's dispatch is a closed set of four paths (run_one
#                 and grep -c mutate_ over all 23 of those commands finds three
#             (3) execve traces (strace -f -s 300) of one row of the run_one
#                 kind and one of the run_graygate kind: 0 mutate execs, while
#                 the SAME graygate trace shows 25 execs of sim/gray_check.sh.
#                 (3) is the discrimination test; (1) and (2) alone are a grep.
# exitcontract  VERDICT  = exits non-zero when a mutant's verdict differs from
#                          the one written down for it.  Only these can be a
#                          gate row that catches a lost property.
#               ANCHOR   = exits non-zero only when a row failed to RUN (a dead
#                          anchor) or a Z0 self-teeth row stopped firing.  Real
#                          value, but not the value the name suggests.
#               NONE     = the last executable statement is an echo, so the
#                          script exits 0 whatever it printed.  52 of 63.
# runtime     MEASURED by /usr/bin/time -v, serial, one at a time; '-' = not
#             measured.  Do NOT infer one from the bench: mutate_swiglu_mem.sh
#             is 495.8 s and mutate_rmsnorm_bf_mem.sh 46.0 s for the same shape.
# liveness    from a 30 s sweep, 2026-09-20.  OK = ran to its own summary;
#             DEAD = exited non-zero having produced no table; DEADROWS = ran,
#             but printed ANCHOR FAILED for one or more rows; TIMEOUT(30s) = did
#             not finish in 30 s, which is NOT evidence that it is alive.
